content: OneDrive driveItem addressing / path encoding (Microsoft Learn, updated 2026-05-14). Path addressing form: /drive/root:/Documents/MyFile.xlsx:/content - everything between the two colons is a path relative to the preceding item. Equivalent forms: /drive/items/{id}/content, /drives/{drive-id}/items/{item-id}/content, /drive/special/documents:/file:/content. OneDrive reserved characters (cannot appear in names): / \ * < > ? : | ; OneDrive for BUSINESS additionally reserves # and %. Folder names cannot end with a period; business names cannot start with ~. Graph expects RFC 3986. Allowed unencoded path characters are pchar = unreserved / pct-encoded / sub-delims / ':' / '@' where unreserved = ALPHA DIGIT - . _ ~ and sub-delims = ! $ & ' ( ) * + , ; = . Characters outside pchar - notably '#' and space - MUST be percent-encoded (space -> %20, # -> %23, literal % -> %25). Explicit warning: you cannot URL-encode a whole URL in one call because encoding rules differ per segment; encode only the path portion. Worked examples: /root:/Ryan's%20Files , /root:/Break%23Out , /root:/Ryan's%20Files/estimate%25s.docx . Note apostrophe is a sub-delim and is legal unencoded in a PATH, but inside an OData string literal such as search(q='...') a single quote must be doubled ('').
